title: How to Force Windows to Detect Display
overview: Use Windows display controls to detect a connected external monitor and select the correct projection mode. These checks help distinguish a Windows display-setting problem from a cable, port, adapter, or monitor problem.
checklist: Save open work and confirm you are working on the intended device.

On your Windows computer, press `Win + P` and try cycling through different projection modes (e.g., Duplicate, Extend, Second screen only). Then, open Display Settings (Right-click desktop > Display settings), scroll down, and click 'Detect' under the 'Multiple displays' section.
Record what changed and return to the workflow before making additional changes.
common_indicators: The monitor has power but does not appear in Windows Display settings.
Windows shows only the built-in display.
The monitor displays no image after being connected.
The image appears only after changing the Windows projection mode.

quiz.question: Where can you ask Windows to detect a connected monitor that does not appear automatically?
answers: Settings > System > Display > Multiple displays > Detect
Control Panel > Programs > Uninstall a program
quiz.correct_answer: Settings > System > Display > Multiple displays > Detect
